::: {.lesson-meta}
[Agents]{.pill .t-agents} [Long-Term Agentic Memory · Lesson 5]{.pill .muted}
:::

::: {.tldr}
Procedural memory is the agent's **instructions**. Instead of hard-coding the prompts, keep them **in the store** and read them at every run. Then let a **prompt optimizer** rewrite them from feedback like *"Always sign your emails John Doe"*. The agent learns how to behave without anyone editing code.
:::

## The loop

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S[("Store<br/>agent_instructions<br/>triage_ignore / notify / respond")] -->|"read at runtime"| A[Email agent]
  A --> C[Conversation]
  C --> O[Prompt optimizer]
  F[/User feedback/] --> O
  O -->|"write updated prompts"| S
```

## Key ideas

::: {.concepts}
::: {.concept}
`Prompts as data`

Each prompt is a store item: key `agent_instructions`, value `{"prompt": "..."}`.
:::
::: {.concept}
`Defaults on first run`

If a key is missing (new user), write the default prompt to the store and use it.
:::
::: {.concept}
`Multi-prompt optimizer`

Feedback is about the whole agent. The optimizer works out **which** prompts to change, and **how**.
:::
::: {.concept}
`Background update`

Optimisation runs after the conversation, outside the agent's response.
:::
:::

## Reading prompts from the store

```python
def get_prompt(store, user_id, key, default):
    item = store.get((user_id,), key)
    if item is None:                                   # first run for this user
        store.put((user_id,), key, {"prompt": default})
        return default
    return item.value["prompt"]
```

**In the triage router**, read the three triage rules before formatting the system prompt:

```python
def triage_router(state: State, config: RunnableConfig, store: BaseStore) -> Command[...]:
    user_id = config["configurable"]["langgraph_user_id"]
    ignore_prompt  = get_prompt(store, user_id, "triage_ignore",  default_triage_rules["ignore"])
    notify_prompt  = get_prompt(store, user_id, "triage_notify",  default_triage_rules["notify"])
    respond_prompt = get_prompt(store, user_id, "triage_respond", default_triage_rules["respond"])
    ...
```

**In the response agent**, build the system prompt dynamically:

```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import dynamic_prompt, ModelRequest
from langgraph.config import get_config, get_store

@dynamic_prompt
def agent_prompt(request: ModelRequest) -> str:
    user_id = get_config()["configurable"]["langgraph_user_id"]
    instructions = get_prompt(get_store(), user_id, "agent_instructions", default_agent_instructions)
    return agent_system_prompt_memory.format(instructions=instructions, **profile)

response_agent = create_agent(
    "openai:gpt-5.4-mini",
    tools=[write_email, schedule_meeting, check_calendar_availability,
           manage_memory_tool, search_memory_tool],
    middleware=[agent_prompt],
    store=store,
)
```

Because prompts are read **at runtime**, any update in the store applies to the next run.

## Optimizing prompts from feedback

```python
from langmem import create_multi_prompt_optimizer

optimizer = create_multi_prompt_optimizer("anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5", kind="prompt_memory")

conversations = [(response["messages"], "Always sign your emails `John Doe`")]

prompts = [
    {"name": "main_agent",
     "prompt": store.get(("lance",), "agent_instructions").value["prompt"],
     "update_instructions": "keep the instructions short and to the point",
     "when_to_update": "Update this prompt whenever there is feedback on how the agent should write emails or schedule events"},
    {"name": "triage-ignore",
     "prompt": store.get(("lance",), "triage_ignore").value["prompt"],
     "update_instructions": "keep the instructions short and to the point",
     "when_to_update": "Update this prompt whenever there is feedback on which emails should be ignored"},
    # … same for "triage-notify" and "triage-respond"
]

updated = optimizer.invoke({"trajectories": conversations, "prompts": prompts})
```

How the optimizer works:

1. It reads each `when_to_update` and decides **which prompts** the feedback concerns.
2. For those prompts only, it applies `update_instructions` to write a **new version**.
3. It returns the list of prompts in the same format.

## Writing the changes back

```python
keys = {"main_agent": "agent_instructions", "triage-ignore": "triage_ignore",
        "triage-notify": "triage_notify", "triage-respond": "triage_respond"}

for old, new in zip(prompts, updated):
    if new["prompt"] != old["prompt"]:
        store.put(("lance",), keys[new["name"]], {"prompt": new["prompt"]})
```

| Feedback | Prompt changed | Effect on the next run |
|---|---|---|
| "Always sign your emails John Doe" | `agent_instructions` | Emails end with the John Doe signature |
| "Ignore any emails from Alice Jones" | `triage_ignore` | Alice's emails are now ignored |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- Procedural memory = **the prompt**, stored as data and read at every run.
- Always provide **defaults**, so a new user works with no setup.
- The multi-prompt optimizer maps one piece of feedback to the **right prompt(s)**: `when_to_update` decides which, `update_instructions` decides how.
- Re-read prompts from the store before each optimisation, so you start from the latest version.
- `kind="prompt_memory"` is the simplest optimizer. LangMem also offers `metaprompt` and `gradient`.
:::

## Quiz

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Why read prompts from the store at runtime instead of loading them once?</summary>
<p>So that an update written by the optimizer applies to the very next run, with no restart or code change.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>The feedback is "Ignore emails from Alice Jones". Why does only <code>triage_ignore</code> change?</summary>
<p>The optimizer compares the feedback with each prompt's <code>when_to_update</code>, and only the ignore rule matches.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Which memory type is this, and is it updated in the hot path or in the background?</summary>
<p>Procedural memory, updated in the background after the conversation.</p>
</details>
